title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for diabetes and neuropathy.

HPI: [Copied forward from previous visit] Patient is an 88-year-old female presenting for management of type 2 diabetes and chronic peripheral neuropathy. She reports stable symptoms with current regimen.

Update: Patient reports she is continuing her long-term medications without significant side effects. She notes some tingling in her feet but states it remains stable. She denies any new acute symptoms or changes in her mobility.

Vitals: BP 128/80, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F, Weight 145 lbs.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative
Neurological: Positive (numbness in feet)
Musculoskeletal: Negative
Skin: Negative
All other systems reviewed and negative.

Medication List:
- Insulin and oral hypoglycemic (glipizide)
- Gabapentin

Exam:
General: Well-appearing, alert and oriented x3.
Neurological: Symmetrical muscle strength. Diminished sensation to light touch in bilateral toes.
Skin: Intact, no ulcers noted.

Assessment:
1. Type 2 diabetes: Stable on current insulin and oral hypoglycemic medications.
2. Polyneuropathy: Chronic condition. It is noted that this is unrelated to diabetes.

Plan:
Continue current insulin and oral hypoglycemic regimen. Continue gabapentin for neuropathy. Follow up in 3 months.

Electronically signed, T. Haddad, DO, 05/12/2026
explanations: The provider states the polyneuropathy is not diabetic: code diabetes without complications and the polyneuropathy separately.
Polyneuropathy not due to diabetes is coded separately (G62.9 when no cause is specified).
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Documentation of another cause overrides the 'with' presumption.
The polyneuropathy still needs its own code.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
